definition: Segmenting objects with iterative user input — clicks, scribbles, boxes — where the model refines masks from sparse guidance.
details: Segmenting objects with iterative user input — clicks, scribbles, boxes — where the model refines masks from sparse guidance. It powers annotation tools and photo editing.

explainer.lead: Interactive segmentation produces object masks from sparse user guidance such as clicks, scribbles, or boxes, refined over successive rounds. It matters because it makes precise mask creation fast for people who are not training models.

tiers.eli5: You click a few spots on an object and the computer colours in the rest, then you nudge it until the outline is right.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers deploy these models inside annotation tools and photo editors, feeding each user click back as input to refine the mask. A pitfall is that repeated refinement can drift from the user's intent when guidance is very sparse.
tiers.paperLevel: The task is segmenting objects with iterative user input (clicks, scribbles, boxes), where the model refines masks from sparse guidance over repeated interaction.

explainer.example: A user places one click on a person and one on the background; the model returns a mask, and a correcting click on a stray region tightens the boundary.
